messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Consydre This is an archaic moral plea: the speaker asks for consideration of his own condition and of his father's helplessness, then poses a rhetorical question about not abandoning him. Consydre
Analysis In modern English, it means the speaker should reflect on his blind, poor, infirm father and on his own power to make the father's remaining years comfortable, implying that forsaking him would be unjust. Analysis
Tone The tone is ethical and emotional, contrasting filial duty and pity with abandonment, and presenting comfort and joy as the proper end for the father's final years. Tone
